# Close the Cloud <-> Data Center reconciler test-parity gaps

## Why this exists

Two Jira adapters now sit behind one backend port, and they were hardened at different times by
different means:

* **Cloud** (`adapters/jira/`, ACLI-based) is the historically battle-tested path. Years of
  production incidents produced byte-for-byte characterization pins, ADF depth tests, comment and
  description length-convergence suites, and a large applier/differ corpus.
* **Data Center** (`adapters/jira_datacenter/`, pycontribs-based) was written and tested intensively
  during epic [rebar:e369-a449-4773-48fb], which drove it against a real Dockerized instance. That
  work produced things Cloud never had: multi-page pagination proofs, a 429/`Retry-After` matrix,
  TLS and credential validation, a live 49-cell harness suite, and a structural anti-regression
  guard.

**The gaps therefore run in BOTH directions, and that is the point of this epic.** A parity audit
commissioned while closing e369 found Cloud-only coverage that DC lacks AND DC-only coverage that
Cloud lacks — and the second direction contains the single highest-risk finding, because Cloud's
whole-project readers have never been tested past one page while DC's have.

## The governing insight

Every defect e369 found in the DC adapter was an OPERATIONAL EDGE that only appears against a
differently-configured instance: index lag, server-side page caps, admin-toggled rate limiting,
screen configuration, workflow transition naming. None was an architectural flaw. The same class of
edge exists on Cloud and is simply untested there, because Cloud's coverage grew from *incidents
that happened* rather than from *configurations that differ*.

So this epic is not "make the two suites look alike". It is: **for each behaviour the two adapters
share, the harder-won test should exist on both sides**, and where a SHARED module is exercised
through only one adapter, a regression must not be able to reach production for the other.

## Scope

Test-tier work plus the small production changes that untested duplication forces (one map is
genuinely duplicated and must be single-sourced before it can be guarded). No behaviour change to
either adapter is intended; where a test reveals one is needed, that becomes its own bug ticket
rather than being folded in silently.

## Out of scope

Adding coverage for behaviours only one adapter HAS (Cloud's ADF codec depth, DC's TLS/PAT
handling) — those are legitimate asymmetries, not gaps. Promoting `_engine` through the mypy
strictness ratchet. Any change to the backend port's shape.

## Provenance

Commissioned during epic e369's closeout. Every finding below was verified against the tree before
being written down — the audit was treated as a lead, not as evidence.

## PRIORITY FRAMING (operator direction, 2026-08-02) — READ THIS BEFORE PICKING UP A CHILD

The top priority is **shipping defect-free Jira Data Center functionality.** This epic is a
*related* priority precisely because parity is what gives confidence that the DC feature is
defect-free — it is instrumental to the goal, not adjacent to it.

That ranks the two directions differently, and the ranking should drive which child you take:

* **DC-DIRECTION GAPS COME FIRST.** `cedc` (DC characterization) and `79d5` (DC length convergence
  + the comment ceiling) are the ones that directly buy confidence in what is being shipped. DC's
  values have never been pinned; its contract test asserts SHAPE only and would pass with every
  value wrong. Until those land, "the DC adapter is defect-free" rests on the live harness alone,
  and the live harness only covers the configurations that one default-configured instance happens
  to have.
* **BOTH-DIRECTION items rank with them** where they touch DC: `bd9e` (the duplicated ticket-type
  map is read by DC's create path) and `2944` (several of the tests that cannot fail are DC tests,
  so they are confidence we do not actually have).
* **CLOUD-DIRECTION GAPS RANK BELOW.** `0fad` and `2127` harden the mature, live-exercised Cloud
  path. They are real and worth doing — `0fad` in particular is a genuine latent truncation risk —
  but they do not serve the DC-confidence goal, and they must not gate it. `0fad` was moved out of
  epic e369 for exactly this reason and dropped to P2 under this framing.

**Do not read "parity" as "make the two suites symmetrical."** The goal is confidence in the DC
feature. Where an asymmetry is legitimate (Cloud's ADF depth, DC's TLS/PAT handling) closing it buys
nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cedc-58d1-f6d1-428e` is closed: DC's create-path field values, both sanitizer boundaries,
      the identity label form, and all four probe branches are pinned BY VALUE, and the shared
      `map_fields_to_remote` body is exercised through `WikiTextCodec` as well as `AdfCodec`
- [ ] `79d5-63c7-5f31-48a7` is closed: an oversized DC comment AND an oversized DC description each
      converge across TWO passes (pass 2 plans nothing for that ticket), and the real DC comment
      ceiling is either measured-and-recorded on the ticket or explicitly marked UNVERIFIED at the
      `max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` binding
- [ ] `bd9e-0740-1b47-47f8` is closed: exactly ONE dict literal defines the local->Jira ticket-type
      map within `adapters/`, and `test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` carries an assertion that
      fails the build if a second copy appears — the same guard shape the status and priority maps
      already have
- [ ] `2944-dd3f-e982-4359` is closed: each of the five enumerated vacuous tests either asserts the
      contract its own docstring names or is renamed to what it actually pins; none is merely
      deleted, because the docstring's intent is the valuable part
- [ ] [operator-attested] every pin or rewrite added under this epic is MUTATION-CHECKED — the
      mutation applied and the resulting verdict recorded as a comment on the owning child ticket. A
      pin nobody has seen fail is not evidence. Copied terminal output showing the mutated code and
      the resulting FAIL, pasted as a child-ticket comment, satisfies this criterion; it is attested
      rather than CI-checkable because a mutation is applied and reverted in a working tree and
      therefore leaves no repo artifact to inspect
- [ ] where the two adapters CORRECTLY diverge, the expectation carries a DIFFERENT value per
      vendor rather than asserting sameness. Checked positively rather than as a negative property:
      the parametrized characterization suite must contain at least one case for EACH known
      divergence — (a) rich text, ADF vs wiki markup, and (b) identity form, Cloud `accountId` vs
      DC `name` — in which the Cloud and DC parameters carry DIFFERENT expected values, and both
      cases pass. Verifiable by reading the parametrize table in the diff and by running those
      cases; a reviewer can confirm it without re-deriving which behaviours diverge, because the
      two are enumerated here
- [ ] `test_backend_characterization.py`'s pre-existing Cloud assertions still pass UNEDITED, so
      Cloud's incident-hardened safety net is intact rather than loosened to fit DC
- [ ] the P2 Cloud-direction children (`0fad-59f7-1605-4377`, `2127-348c-c41d-472e`) are explicitly
      NOT required for the DC-confidence goal and do not gate it; they close on their own merit
